body:
Order of composition events is: 

Chrome: `compositionstart` -> ...  -> `compositionupdate` -> `input` -> `compositionend`(vue fires a sync` input`) 

Firefox: `compositionstart` -> ... -> `compositionupdate` -> `compositionend`(vue fires a sync` input`) -> `input`

So `v-model` set value twice  in Firefox, which is redundant. 

This PR fixes bug via only firing a `input` in  `compositionend` which immediately follows `compositionupdate` -> `input`.
author: xiaodemen

body:
Native behavior:

```
// Chrome
start ... update ... input ... end
          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ last composition

// Firefox
start ... update ... end ... input
          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ last composition
```

Because we want to ignore `input` events during composition on `v-model`, current behavior always dispatches an `input` event after `compositionend` otherwise we won't get notified after composition end:

```
// Chrome
[start ... update ... input ... end] ... input (by Vue)
                      ~~~~~ ignored      ~~~~~ triggered

// Firefox
[start ... update ... end] ... input (by Vue) ... input
                               ~~~~~ triggered    ~~~~~ triggered
```

So in Firefox we will get two consecutive `input` events triggered with same value.

This fix watches the `compositionupdate` & `input` event sequence during composition, and only dispatch an `input` event when `compositionend` is immediately following a `compositionupdate` event, not an `input` event. So now it becomes:

```
// Chrome
[start ... update ... input ... end] ... input (by Vue)
                      ~~~~~ ignored      ~~~~~ triggered

// Firefox
[start ... update ... end] ... (removed) ... input
                                             ~~~~~ triggered
```

$ npm pack

Now let's apply my patch:

```
$ echo ".npmignore" >> src/.npmignore

Node has legitimate APIs to create a new running environment (context) for sandboxing or something else if you want. Changing the global `Date` variable by the user is usually a bad idea and should be prohibited strictly, but I think this is not a case because it is done automatically/internally/implicitly by Node/v8 itself. Although the two `Date`s are valid native `Date` constructors for Node/v8, Vue type checking relies on the current global constructor to identify whether it is an instance of `Date` or not, thus it fails.
